question: An Rh-negative woman undergoes a first-trimester surgical termination of pregnancy at 10 weeks. She is unsensitised (indirect Coombs test negative). Which is the correct anti-D immunoglobulin regimen?

answers.text: 250 IU anti-D within 72 hours of the procedure

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. For sensitising events up to 20 weeks gestation (including TOP, miscarriage, amniocentesis), 250 IU anti-D must be given within 72 hours. If >20 weeks, 500 IU is required.

answers.text: 500 IU anti-D within 72 hours of the procedure

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: 500 IU is the dose for sensitising events after 20 weeks gestation. At 10 weeks, 250 IU is appropriate.

answers.text: 250 IU anti-D within 1 week of the procedure

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The timing is critical — anti-D must be administered within 72 hours of the sensitising event, not within a week, to prevent immunisation.

answers.text: No anti-D is needed as the pregnancy was in the first trimester

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: This is incorrect and dangerous. Sensitisation can occur from as early as 7–8 weeks; anti-D prophylaxis is required from 10 weeks onwards for any sensitising event.

overallFeedback.feedback: At <20 weeks: 250 IU anti-D within 72 hours. At ≥20 weeks: 500 IU within 72 hours. Never delay beyond 72 hours after any sensitising event.
Correct. <20 weeks = 250 IU within 72 hours; ≥20 weeks = 500 IU within 72 hours. Timing is non-negotiable.
